Hi Chandler — thanks for the clear list. Short answer and next steps below, longer formal SLA proposal attached.

Summary (high-level):
- Throughput commitment: we guarantee baseline throughput for the reserved pool expressed as sustained tokens/sec per GPU equivalence and a derived requests/sec target for common request sizes. Baseline numbers and test methodology in the attached SLA PDF.
- Overflow behavior: Dedicated pools are isolated (no cross-customer preemption). When demand exceeds the reserved baseline we offer two configured behaviors: (1) queue up to a configurable request backlog, or (2) automatically burst to shared capacity for short windows. You can pick policy per route.
- Queue limits & latency: default queue depth is 1,000 requests across the pool (configurable). Expected p95 latency under baseline load: ~150–300ms for short (<256 token) responses; p99 targets are in the SLA table. During sustained overload we recommend burst-with-throttling to avoid unbounded queues.
- Credits: SLA credits are tiered by percentage of uptime / latency SLO misses; proposal includes credit schedule and remediation steps.

Next steps: I attached our RDW-SLA-proposal-v3.pdf and a starter capacity worksheet (ornatek-dedicated-plan.xlsx). Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your SREs to walk through numbers. Suggested times: Thu 11/07 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 11/08 14:00–15:00 PT. Which works?

Marissa — below is what I recommend we commit to for Ornatek's 8-GPU reservation. I copied the language we should include in the SLA doc (we can hand this to Legal for final phrasing).

Engineered guarantee (technical summary):
- Baseline throughput: Redwood commits to a baseline sustained throughput equivalent to X tokens/sec per vGPU. For Ornatek (8 vGPU equivalence) this maps to a sustained baseline of 850k tokens/min (approx 14.1k tokens/sec) measured using our standard 256-token median request profile via the RDW throughput harness (test harness link in the SLA). We also provide an expected requests/sec baseline for the customer's median request size (see attachment table).
- Latency SLOs: Under baseline load the service will meet p50/p95/p99 generational latency targets for short requests (<256 tokens): p50 ~70–120ms, p95 ~220–320ms, p99 <750ms. We include a separate table for longer requests.

Overflow and queueing policy:
- Isolation: Dedicated pools are isolated; they are not preempted by hosted traffic.
- Configurable overflow policies (per-route):
  * Queue: default queue depth = 1,000 requests (cluster-wide). Queue policy will keep requests in FIFO order and attach an estimated wait-time header to each queued request. If a request exceeds the configurable max-wait (default 60s) it will be dropped with a 429 and tertiary routing option will be triggered if configured (e.g., route to smaller model variant).
  * Burst: customers can opt-in to burst behavior which allows short-term borrowing from a shared overflow capacity up to 2x baseline throughput for windows up to 10 minutes; bursts are metered and billed at premium rate.
  * Reject: for strict tail-latency SLAs customers can elect a strict reject policy (no queueing) which returns 503 when capacity is exhausted.
- Fallbacks: Automatic fallbacks to quantized/smaller model variants are supported but must be configured as a routing policy; Redwood will not silently swap models without explicit customer rules.

Measurement & credits:
- Measurement: we measure uptime and latency SLOs at the route token granularity with a 5-minute evaluation window and monthly aggregation for credit calculations. The SLA doc contains test harness and measurement definitions.
- Credits: tiered credit schedule: 1–3 hours/month below SLO => 5% monthly credit on dedicated fee; 3–12 hours => 15%; >12 hours => 35%. Latency misses trigger scoped credits on affected routes. Legal should limit absolute credit cap to monthly dedicated fee.

Operational notes and edge cases:
- Maintenance: scheduled maintenance windows will be provided 7 days in advance and are excluded from uptime calc if within notified window.
- Hardware failure: in the event of a node failure Redwood will attempt automatic failover to spare capacity in the same region; if we cannot restore to baseline within 2 hours the credit schedule above applies.

I attached the SLA wording (RDW-SLA-proposal-v3.pdf) and the capacity worksheet with derived numbers for 8 vGPU equivalence (ornatek-dedicated-plan.xlsx). If procurement wants narrower p99 guarantees we should move to a higher committed GPU count or accept a stricter reject policy.

—Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW-SLA-proposal-v3.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

SLA summary (for insertion into procurement packet):
- Baseline throughput: Redwood guarantees a sustained baseline equivalent to ~850k tokens/min for an 8 vGPU reservation (measurement: RDW throughput harness, 256-token median request).
- Latency SLOs (baseline): p50 ~70–120ms, p95 ~220–320ms, p99 <750ms for short responses (<256 tokens).
- Overflow behavior: Dedicated pools are isolated. You can choose per-route policy: Queue (default, 1,000 request cluster depth, default max-wait 60s), Burst (borrow up to 2x baseline for windows up to 10 minutes, billed), or Reject (strict tail-latency protection). Automatic fallback to smaller/quantized models is available if configured.
- Credits & measurement: Monthly aggregation; tiered credit schedule (5%/15%/35% for increasing downtime buckets). Detailed measurement method and caps are in the attached SLA.
- Operational items: scheduled maintenance notification (>=7 days), hardware-failure failover attempts and a 2-hour restoration credit trigger.
